This is expected behavior in the **Xcode Simulator / sandbox testing environment**. StoreKit testing (either with a StoreKit Configuration file or the sandbox) auto-approves purchases without showing the real Apple payment sheet.

**On a real device with a real App Store subscription**, users will always see the standard Apple confirmation dialog (Face ID / Touch ID / password prompt) before being charged. There's no code issue here — this is just how the simulator works.

If you want to verify the dialog flow more realistically, you can test on a **physical device with a sandbox Apple ID**, which will show a simplified version of the confirmation prompt.

why is the apple watch not showing i need to run it

The Apple Watch simulators aren't showing in the Xcode run destination picker because you have the **Taptic** (iOS) scheme selected. To run the watch app:

1. Click the scheme selector at the top (where it says **"Taptic"** next to the device picker)
2. Switch to the **"Taptic Watch Watch App"** scheme
3. The watch simulators will then appear as run destinations

The watch simulators exist (your second screenshot from Window > Devices & Simulators confirms that), they just don't show as destinations for an iOS scheme — only for the watchOS scheme.
